contexts: 610-bed teaching hospital with audit and feedback on medical wards
surgical wards and intensive care without it
two community hospitals with telephone advice only
2.4 pharmacist FTE for the whole network
reading: The committee's disagreement follows the two strands. Measured outcomes show a modest effect on use that depends on delivery and staffing (claims c1, c2, c5) and are reported with incompatible measures (claim c6). Experience evidence explains why: recommendations work when they arrive on time, in person, from a trusted team member, and when nurses carry them (claims c3, c4, c7). Extending written feedback to surgery, intensive care and small hospitals with the same staff is exactly where both strands predict weak acceptance.
